description: Walks the whole fund area in SharePoint, finds every investor entity and every investment folder beneath it, and builds the investment register spreadsheet: a row for each investment, with the investor entity, what was invested in, the asset type and what is held, the commitment and what is still unfunded, the first investment date, the term, tax status, liquidity, currency, website, what the business does and what was bought. AI reads the documents in each folder and is asked three questions per investment: what was bought, the terms, then the descriptions. A question it cannot finish answering costs only its own columns. Folder and file names settle the commitment and the first investment date wherever they state them, so those figures read the same on every run. Every cell already filled in by hand is carried over and only the empty ones are written. A second sheet lists the gaps and queries: empty drawers, folders with no valuation, folder names that break the naming convention, a payment filed against an investment smaller than the payment, documents that could not be read, and the same folder name used under two entities. The spreadsheet it was built from is never written to: each run saves a new file beside it with the day in its name. The register also goes to Reports as a web page and a copy is kept in Knowledge.

# -- Walk the fund area and find every entity and every investment folder under it --
import re

SP = "m365-sharepoint"
MAX_ITEMS = 1500
MAX_DEPTH = 6
# How deep below the link to look for investment folders, and how many folders may be opened doing it.
FIND_DEPTH = 3
FIND_OPENS = 150
MAX_INVESTMENTS = 40
READABLE = {"docx", "docm", "xlsx", "xlsm", "pptx", "pptm", "pdf", "doc", "xls", "ppt", "rtf", "odt", "ods", "odp",
            "txt", "csv", "tsv", "md", "htm", "html"}

# Folder names that are drawers of documents inside one investment, rather than investments in their own right.
DRAWER_WORDS = ["capital call", "drawdown", "draw down", "quarterly", "annual", "report", "statement", "tax",
                "dividend", "distribution", "application", "subscription", "deed", "agreement", "due diligence",
                "correspondence", "letter", "email", "notice", "minutes", "certificate", "valuation", "update",
                "newsletter", "legal", "admin", "signed", "scan", "financials", "capital account"]
DRAWER_NAMES = ["dd", "ic", "docs", "misc", "other"]

# What each file is about, so the register reads the documents that carry its columns first.
CATEGORIES = [
    ("Terms and deeds", ["information memorandum", "memorandum", "prospectus", "offer document", "application",
                         "subscription", "deed", "agreement", "declaration", "constitution", "trust deed",
                         "term sheet", "side letter", "allotment", "certificate"]),
    ("Valuations", ["capital account", "valuation", "wealth statement", "unit statement", "statement of account",
                    "holding statement", "nav"]),
    ("Payments", ["eft", "remittance", "funds flow", "receipt", "capital call", "drawdown", "draw down",
                  "call notice", "capital contribution", "invest in"]),
    ("Tax statements", ["tax", "amit", "amma"]),
    ("Investor updates", ["update", "newsletter", "quarterly", "investor", "shareholder", "presentation",
                          "annual report", "financial statement", "summary", "overview"]),
    ("Distributions", ["dividend", "distribution", "payment advice"]),
]
READ_ORDER = ["Terms and deeds", "Valuations", "Payments", "Tax statements", "Investor updates", "Distributions",
              "Other documents"]

# $400K and $1M are how the folders are named; $527,000 and $1,135,000 are how the documents are.
AMOUNT_IN_NAME = re.compile(r"\$\s?(\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+(?:\.\d{2})?|\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s?([KkMm])?(?![\d%])")
MONTH_IN_NAME = re.compile(r"^((?:19|20)\d{2})[ ._-](0[1-9]|1[0-2])\b")
DAY_IN_NAME = re.compile(r"(19|20)(\d{2})[ ._-](0?[1-9]|1[0-2])[ ._-](0?[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])(?!\d)")


_CACHE = {}


def _ext(name):
    m = re.search(r"\.([A-Za-z0-9]+)$", str(name or ""))
    return m.group(1).lower() if m else ""


def _err(exc):
    msg = str(exc)
    if msg.startswith("tool_error: "):
        msg = msg[len("tool_error: "):]
    if "no usable credential" in msg or "credential unavailable" in msg:
        return "the SharePoint connection needs connecting (Settings - Connections - m365-sharepoint)"
    return msg[:300]


def _list(args):
    out = []
    folder = {}
    cursor = None
    while True:
        page = api.connectors.invoke(server=SP, tool="list_sharepoint_folder",
                                     args={"cursor": cursor} if cursor else dict(args, page_size=200))
        if not isinstance(page, dict):
            raise ValueError("SharePoint sent back something unexpected")
        if not cursor:
            folder = page.get("folder") or {}
        out.extend(page.get("items") or [])
        cursor = page.get("nextCursor")
        if not cursor or len(out) >= MAX_ITEMS:
            return folder, out


def _is_drawer(name):
    low = str(name or "").strip().lower()
    if low in DRAWER_NAMES:
        return True
    for w in DRAWER_WORDS:
        if w in low:
            return True
    return False


def _kids(f):
    """The folders inside one folder. Cached, because the same folder is asked about up to three times."""
    key = str(f.get("id") or "")
    if key not in _CACHE:
        _, items = _list({"drive_id": f.get("driveId"), "item_id": f.get("id")})
        _CACHE[key] = [i for i in items if i.get("isFolder")]
    return _CACHE[key]


def _looks_investment(f):
    """Reads as an investment: not a drawer, and either names an amount or holds drawers of its own."""
    name = str(f.get("name") or "")
    if _is_drawer(name):
        return False
    if re.search(r"\$\s?\d", name):
        return True
    for k in _kids(f):
        if _is_drawer(str(k.get("name") or "")):
            return True
    return False


def _is_investment(f):
    """An investment only when nothing inside it is an investment too.

    An entity folder reads as an investment on its own - it holds Distributions, Reports and Tax, which are
    drawers - so asking only what a folder looks like makes every entity one blended investment. A folder
    holding investments is the container for them, never one of them.

    A name that states an amount settles it on the spot. "2024 09 Capital Investments - Head Co $527K" holds
    a "Head Co Investment" folder inside it, and looking inside first picked that one and lost the amount,
    the month and the investment's real name along with it."""
    if not _looks_investment(f):
        return False
    if re.search(r"\$\s?\d", str(f.get("name") or "")):
        return True
    for k in _kids(f):
        if _looks_investment(k):
            return False
    return True


def _category(name, parent):
    for text in (str(name or "").lower(), "/" + str(parent or "").lower() + "/"):
        for label, words in CATEGORIES:
            if any(w in text for w in words):
                return label
    return "Other documents"


def _named_amount(name):
    """The money a name states, or None when it states none or states more than one figure."""
    found = AMOUNT_IN_NAME.findall(str(name or ""))
    if len(found) != 1:
        return None
    raw, unit = found[0]
    try:
        n = float(raw.replace(",", ""))
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if unit and unit.lower() == "k":
        n = n * 1000
    elif unit and unit.lower() == "m":
        n = n * 1000000
    return n


def _named_month(name):
    m = MONTH_IN_NAME.search(str(name or "").strip())
    return m.group(1) + "-" + m.group(2) if m else ""


def _named_day(name):
    m = DAY_IN_NAME.search(str(name or "").rsplit("/", 1)[-1])
    return m.group(1) + m.group(2) + "-" + m.group(3).zfill(2) + "-" + m.group(4).zfill(2) if m else ""


link = str(params.get("folder_link") or "").strip()
pick = str(params.get("entity_name") or "").strip().lower()

investments = []
top_name = ""
top_url = ""
problem = ""

if not link:
    problem = ("No folder link: paste the SharePoint link of the folder that holds the entity folders "
               "(Share then Copy link) when you click Run now.")
else:
    try:
        top, items = _list({"url": link})
        top_name = str(top.get("name") or "")
        top_url = str(top.get("webUrl") or link)
        # Find the investment folders. The entity is whichever folder sits directly below the link; when the
        # link is an entity folder itself, its own name is the entity.
        search = [(i, 1, "", "") for i in items if i.get("isFolder")]
        opened = 0
        while search and opened < FIND_OPENS and len(investments) < MAX_INVESTMENTS:
            cand, level, ent, ent_url = search.pop(0)
            name = str(cand.get("name") or "")
            opened += 1
            if _is_drawer(name):
                continue
            if _is_investment(cand):
                investments.append({
                    "entity_folder": ent or top_name,
                    "entity_url": ent_url or top_url,
                    "folder": name,
                    "folder_url": str(cand.get("webUrl") or ""),
                    "driveId": cand.get("driveId"),
                    "id": cand.get("id"),
                    "named_amount": _named_amount(name),
                    "named_month": _named_month(name),
                })
                continue
            if level < FIND_DEPTH:
                next_ent = ent or (name if level == 1 else "")
                next_url = ent_url or (str(cand.get("webUrl") or "") if level == 1 else "")
                search.extend((s, level + 1, next_ent, next_url) for s in _kids(cand))
        if pick:
            investments = [i for i in investments if pick in str(i["entity_folder"]).lower()]
    except Exception as exc:
        problem = "Couldn't open the folder: " + _err(exc)

# List each investment's files, so the next step knows what there is to read and which drawers are empty.
for inv in investments:
    files = []
    empty = []
    try:
        _, kids = _list({"drive_id": inv["driveId"], "item_id": inv["id"]})
        queue = [(k, "", 1) for k in kids]
        while queue and len(files) < MAX_ITEMS:
            item, parent, depth = queue.pop(0)
            name = str(item.get("name") or "")
            path = (parent + "/" + name) if parent else name
            if item.get("isFolder"):
                if depth < MAX_DEPTH:
                    _, sub = _list({"drive_id": item.get("driveId"), "item_id": item.get("id")})
                    if not sub:
                        empty.append(path)
                    queue.extend((s, path, depth + 1) for s in sub)
                continue
            if name.lower() in (".ds_store", "thumbs.db"):
                continue
            files.append({
                "name": name,
                "path": path,
                "category": _category(name, parent),
                "readable": _ext(name) in READABLE,
                "driveId": item.get("driveId"),
                "id": item.get("id"),
                "day": _named_day(name),
                "amount": _named_amount(name),
            })
    except Exception as exc:
        inv["note"] = "Couldn't list it: " + _err(exc)
    inv["files"] = files
    inv["file_count"] = len(files)
    inv["empty_drawers"] = empty

if not problem and not investments:
    problem = ("No investment folders were found under " + (top_name or "that link") + ". An investment folder "
               "is one that states an amount in its name or holds drawers such as Capital Calls, Reports or Tax.")

entities = []
for inv in investments:
    if inv["entity_folder"] not in entities:
        entities.append(inv["entity_folder"])

summary = (problem if problem else
           "Found " + str(len(investments)) + " investments across " + str(len(entities)) + " entities under " +
           (top_name or "the link") + ", holding " + str(sum(i["file_count"] for i in investments)) + " files.")

outputs.description: Every investment found, with its entity, its folder and its files.

outputs.description: The name of the folder the link points at.

# -- Read each investment's documents and have AI fill the register's columns --
import re
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

SP = "m365-sharepoint"
# Three AI questions per investment, not one per document, so the run costs the same whether a folder holds
# 8 documents or 227.
#
# Three because an AI step is given 1500 output tokens for the whole answer, thinking included, and the model
# thinks in proportion to how much it has been asked. One question covering all fifteen register columns
# never got as far as writing anything: stop_reason=max_tokens, content blocks: thinking, text length 0. Two
# questions got the figures out but never once finished the descriptions. The budget is per question, so
# three smaller questions have more of it between them than one large one has on its own, and each is asked
# over only the documents it needs - reading less to think less - with a ceiling on how long its answers run.
MAX_DOCS = 6
# How far down the list it will go looking for those six. A scanned page has no text in it and cannot be
# known to have none until it has been opened, so the ones that come back empty are passed over rather
# than counted, up to this many attempts.
MAX_TRIES = 14
DOC_TEXT = 3200
# A deed is read far further in than anything else. What a register wants from one - the term, how an
# investor gets their money out, what the thing is for tax - is settled in clauses, and a sixty-page
# limited partnership agreement spends its first few thousand characters on a cover page and recitals.
DEED_TEXT = 150000
DEED_CATEGORY = "Terms and deeds"
FACT_DOCS = 5
FACT_TEXT = 2400
PROSE_DOCS = 3
PROSE_TEXT = 1800
RETRY_DOCS = 2
RETRY_TEXT = 1000
# The terms question is not given documents from the top. It is given the parts of them that talk about
# terms, each with enough either side to read as a sentence, up to what fits under the 32,000-character
# cap on an AI step's prompt and input together.
TERM_WINDOW = 700
TERM_LIMIT = 14000
# Narrow on purpose. A bare "term", "tax" or "commitment" appears on nearly every page of a placement
# memorandum, and matching those spent the whole budget on the front matter - the not-an-offer notice, the
# notice to investors in Australia - before reaching a clause that answers anything. These are the words
# that only turn up where the answer is.
TERM_RE = re.compile(
    # How long it runs. A placement memorandum states this twice: once as a row in the key-terms table
    # ("Term Five years from end of the Investment Period"), once as a clause ("the Partnership has a term
    # of five years"). Both shapes are here, because neither says "term of the fund".
    r"(^[ \t]{0,4}term\b[ :]|\bterm of (?:up to )?(?:[a-z]+|\d+)[- ](?:years?|months?)\b|\bhas a term\b|"
    r"term (?:of the (?:fund|partnership|trust)|may be extended)|(?:fund|partnership|trust) term|"
    r"\bterminat\w+|\bwinding[- ]up\b|\bwound up\b|"
    # How the money comes back out.
    r"\bredemption\b|\bredeem\w*|\bliquidity\b|buy-?backs?|\block-?up\b|\bwithdraw\w+|"
    r"transfer of (?:units|interests|fund interests)|"
    # What it is for tax.
    r"\bESVCLP\b|\bVCLP\b|\bAMIT\b|\bMIT\b|attribution managed investment|pooled development fund|"
    # What is still owed.
    r"\buncalled\b|\bunfunded\b|\bundrawn\b|(?:remaining|total|aggregate) commitment|commitment period|"
    r"\bcapital calls?\b|\bdrawdowns?\b)", re.I | re.M)
READ_ORDER = [DEED_CATEGORY, "Valuations", "Payments", "Tax statements", "Investor updates", "Distributions",
              "Other documents"]

LEAD = (
    "These are the documents a family holds for ONE private investment made by ONE investor entity. "
    "Use only what the documents state. Put null when they do not say it, and never estimate, infer or "
    "fill a field from general knowledge. "
)
# The answer has 1500 tokens to fit in, and whatever the model spends working out loud comes out of the
# same 1500. Both halves of this matter: answer at once, and answer short.
BRIEF = " Write the JSON straight out. Do not reason it through first, and do not explain anything. "

# What was bought. Six columns, all of them names.
WHAT_PROMPT = (
    LEAD + BRIEF +
    "investor_entity is the full legal name of the entity that owns the investment. Where a company holds "
    "it as trustee for a trust, or holds it beneficially for one, give BOTH names joined by ATF, as in "
    "\"Rapaki Pty Ltd ATF Rapaki Share Trust\". Never the trust on its own and never the company on its "
    "own when a document shows the two together, however briefly it says so. "
    "investment_into is the full legal name of the company, fund, trust or partnership the money went into, "
    "with its ABN or ACN in brackets when a document states one. Where the money bought units in a "
    "co-investment trust that in turn holds a company, name the trust, not the company. "
    "asset_type is one word, one of: Fund, Sidecar, Equity, Loan, Property. Sidecar for a single-asset "
    "co-investment trust or a note in one company, Fund for a pooled fund or partnership, Equity for shares. "
    "asset is what is actually held, with the unit or share price when stated, for example \"52,700 fully "
    "paid ordinary shares at A$10.00 per share\". "
    "currency is a short label such as \"Australian dollars (A$)\". "
    "website is the company or fund's own site, never its administrator's, registry's or lawyer's. "
    "No value runs past 25 words."
)
WHAT_SHAPE = (
    '{"investor_entity": str|null, "investment_into": str|null, "asset_type": str|null, "asset": str|null, '
    '"currency": str|null, "website": str|null}'
)

# What was agreed. Six columns, all of them figures, dates or a short phrase.
TERMS_PROMPT = (
    LEAD + BRIEF +
    "commitment is the total the investor entity agreed to put in, as a plain number. "
    "unfunded_commitment is how much of that is still uncalled, as a plain number; 0 when the documents show "
    "it fully drawn. "
    "first_investment is the date the first money went in, YYYY-MM-DD. "
    "term is how long the investment runs, in the documents' own words, for example \"10 years + 2 years\" "
    "or \"no fixed term - ordinary shares\". A fund or partnership almost always states one, so look for "
    "the clause that sets how long it runs and when it is wound up before answering null. Ordinary shares "
    "and convertible notes held directly have no fixed term, and saying so is an answer. "
    "tax_status is the tax structure the documents name for the investment itself - ESVCLP, VCLP, MIT, AMIT, "
    "Pooled Development Fund, unit trust, company - and null when no document names one. A registration "
    "number beginning ILP means a VCLP or ESVCLP: say which the document calls it. "
    "liquidity is how the investor can get their money out, if a document says so, for example \"no "
    "redemptions\" or \"buybacks from 31 December 2029 at the manager's discretion\". A clause saying units "
    "cannot be transferred or redeemed without consent is the answer to this, written plainly. "
    "No value runs past 25 words."
)
TERMS_SHAPE = (
    '{"commitment": number|null, "unfunded_commitment": number|null, "first_investment": "YYYY-MM-DD"|null, '
    '"term": str|null, "tax_status": str|null, "liquidity": str|null}'
)

# The story. Three columns, and the only ones where the model writes rather than copies, so they carry a
# word count: left open, notes alone ran past the budget and took the other two down with it.
PROSE_PROMPT = (
    LEAD + BRIEF +
    "business is what the business or fund does, at most 35 words. "
    "investment is what was bought, when, and how it was paid, at most 35 words. "
    "notes is the one thing a reader of the register most needs to know beyond those - a fee, the trustee or "
    "manager, or something two documents disagree about, in which case follow the later one - at most 35 "
    "words, and null when nothing stands out. "
    "Full sentences, no bullet points, and nothing past those limits."
)
PROSE_SHAPE = '{"business": str|null, "investment": str|null, "notes": str|null}'

# Asked in this order, each over only what it needs: the first and third from the top of the documents
# most likely to carry their columns, the second from the clauses themselves wherever they sit. A question
# that cannot be finished costs its own columns and nothing else, and says so on Gaps and queries.
QUESTIONS = [
    ("what was bought", WHAT_PROMPT, WHAT_SHAPE, "top",
     "The investor entity, what was invested in, the asset type, the asset and the website are empty in this "
     "row, and the folder names stand in for the first two. Fill them in by hand."),
    ("terms", TERMS_PROMPT, TERMS_SHAPE, "clauses",
     "Unfunded commitment, term, tax status and liquidity are empty in this row. The commitment and the first "
     "investment date are unaffected: those come from the folder and file names."),
    ("description", PROSE_PROMPT, PROSE_SHAPE, "prose",
     "The business, the investment and notes are empty in this row. Every figure in it is unaffected."),
]


def _err(exc):
    msg = str(exc)
    if msg.startswith("tool_error: "):
        msg = msg[len("tool_error: "):]
    if "no usable credential" in msg or "credential unavailable" in msg:
        return "the SharePoint connection needs connecting (Settings - Connections - m365-sharepoint)"
    return msg[:200]


def _num(v):
    if isinstance(v, bool) or v is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
        return float(v)
    s = re.sub(r"[,$\s]", "", str(v))
    neg = s.startswith("(") and s.endswith(")")
    try:
        n = float(s.strip("()"))
    except ValueError:
        return None
    return -n if neg else n


def _date(v):
    s = str(v or "")[:10]
    return s if re.match(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$", s) else ""


def _text(v, limit=900):
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(v or "")).strip()
    return s[:limit] if s and s.lower() not in ("null", "none", "n/a", "not stated") else ""


def _symbol(currency):
    # Whole words, not fragments: "Australian" holds "us" and used to print every figure as US dollars.
    low = str(currency or "").lower()
    if "usd" in low or "us dollar" in low or "united states" in low or "american" in low:
        return "US$"
    if "nzd" in low or "new zealand" in low:
        return "NZ$"
    if "eur" in low:
        return "EUR "
    if "gbp" in low or "pound" in low or "sterling" in low:
        return "GBP "
    return "A$"


def _money(amount, currency):
    if amount is None:
        return ""
    return _symbol(currency) + format(int(round(amount)), ",d")


def _day_out(iso):
    return iso[8:10] + "/" + iso[5:7] + "/" + iso[0:4] if _date(iso) else ""


def _month_out(ym):
    if not re.match(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}$", str(ym or "")):
        return ""
    months = ["", "January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September",
              "October", "November", "December"]
    return months[int(ym[5:7])] + " " + ym[0:4]


def _held(iso, today):
    if not _date(iso):
        return ""
    months = (today.year - int(iso[0:4])) * 12 + (today.month - int(iso[5:7]))
    if today.day < int(iso[8:10]):
        months -= 1
    if months < 0:
        return ""
    years, rest = months // 12, months % 12
    if years and rest:
        return str(years) + (" yr " if years == 1 else " yrs ") + str(rest) + " mths"
    if years:
        return str(years) + (" yr" if years == 1 else " yrs")
    return str(rest) + (" mth" if rest == 1 else " mths")


def _pick(files):
    """The documents most likely to carry the register's columns, best first."""
    readable = [f for f in files if f.get("readable")]
    return sorted(readable, key=lambda f: (READ_ORDER.index(f["category"]) if f["category"] in READ_ORDER else 9,
                                           f["name"].lower()))


def _ask(prompt, body, shape):
    got = api.ai.extract(prompt=prompt, input=body, schema_hint=shape)
    return got if isinstance(got, dict) else {}


def _body(head, texts, docs, chars):
    return head + "\n\n".join(t[:chars] for t in texts[:docs])


def _windows(text, budget):
    """The passages of a document that talk about terms, tax and getting money out, each with enough on
    either side of the word to read as a sentence. Overlapping ones are joined rather than repeated."""
    out = []
    used = 0
    end = -1
    for m in TERM_RE.finditer(text):
        start = max(0, m.start() - TERM_WINDOW)
        stop = min(len(text), m.end() + TERM_WINDOW)
        if stop <= end:
            continue
        if start <= end and out:
            out[-1] = out[-1] + text[end:stop]
            used += stop - end
        else:
            out.append(text[start:stop])
            used += stop - start
        end = stop
        if used >= budget:
            break
    return out


def _clauses(head, pages, budget):
    """The terms question's input: the clauses themselves, from however deep in the documents they sit,
    rather than the opening pages of the first few documents. Empty when nothing matched, and the caller
    falls back to reading from the top."""
    parts = []
    used = 0
    for path, text in pages:
        if used >= budget:
            break
        found = _windows(text, budget - used)
        if found:
            parts.append("--- " + path + " ---\n" + "\n [...] \n".join(found))
            used += sum(len(f) for f in found)
    return (head + "\n\n".join(parts)) if parts else ""


def _put(prompt, shape, head, texts, body):
    """One question, and if it cannot be finished, the same question over fewer documents and answered
    shorter. Both of those are the same lever: the less there is to read, the less the model works out
    loud, and the budget it saves is the budget it has left to answer in."""
    try:
        return _ask(prompt, body, shape), ""
    except Exception as exc:
        why = _err(exc)
    try:
        return _ask(prompt + " Ten words at most for every value.",
                    _body(head, texts, RETRY_DOCS, RETRY_TEXT), shape), ""
    except Exception as exc:
        return {}, _err(exc) or why


investments = params.get("investments") or []
# Australian day, not the server's UTC one, so a holding period never reads a day short.
today = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(hours=10)).date()
rows = []
gaps = []
read_count = 0
asked = 0

for inv in investments:
    files = inv.get("files") or []
    folder = str(inv.get("folder") or "")
    entity_folder = str(inv.get("entity_folder") or "")
    # Keep going down the list until MAX_DOCS documents with text in them have been found, rather than
    # taking the first MAX_DOCS and letting the ones that turn out to be scans count against the total.
    # The Finder Side Car folder has four scans in its top six - three trust deeds and the valuation -
    # and taking six meant the questions were answered on two documents instead of six.
    texts = []
    pages = []
    unread = []
    for f in _pick(files)[:MAX_TRIES]:
        if len(texts) >= MAX_DOCS:
            break
        # A deed is read deep, everything else only as far as the register needs. The read costs the same
        # either way: one call per document, whatever is asked of it.
        want = DEED_TEXT if f.get("category") == DEED_CATEGORY else DOC_TEXT
        try:
            r = api.connectors.invoke(server=SP, tool="read_sharepoint_file",
                                      args={"drive_id": f["driveId"], "item_id": f["id"], "max_chars": want})
        except Exception as exc:
            unread.append(f["path"] + " (" + _err(exc) + ")")
            continue
        text = str(r.get("text") or "") if isinstance(r, dict) else ""
        if not text.strip():
            unread.append(f["path"] + " (" + ((str(r.get("note") or "") if isinstance(r, dict) else "") or
                                              "no text could be read from it") + ")")
            continue
        texts.append("--- " + f["path"] + " ---\n" + text[:DOC_TEXT])
        pages.append((f["path"], text[:want]))
        read_count += 1

    head = ("Investor entity folder: " + entity_folder + "\nInvestment folder: " + folder +
            "\nFiles in the folder: " + ", ".join(f["name"] for f in files[:30]) + "\n\n")
    top_body = _body(head, texts, FACT_DOCS, FACT_TEXT)
    bodies = {"top": top_body,
              "clauses": _clauses(head, pages, TERM_LIMIT) or top_body,
              "prose": _body(head, texts, PROSE_DOCS, PROSE_TEXT)}
    got = {}
    for name, prompt, shape, over, cost in QUESTIONS:
        if not texts:
            break
        part, err = _put(prompt, shape, head, texts, bodies[over])
        if err:
            gaps.append([entity_folder + " / " + folder,
                         "AI could not answer the " + name + " question about this investment (" + err + ").",
                         cost])
        else:
            asked += 1
            got.update(part)

    # What the folder and file names state beats what AI read, because a name reads the same on every run.
    currency = _text(got.get("currency"), 60) or "Australian dollars (A$)"
    named = inv.get("named_amount")
    commitment = named if named is not None else _num(got.get("commitment"))
    # A file that names both a day and an amount is a payment; one that names only a day may be anything.
    # "2024 02 05 Year13 Remittance Details" and "2024 04 24 FNC Investor Funds Flow" both read as payments
    # by their names, and both sit months before the money actually moved.
    pays = [f for f in files if f.get("category") == "Payments" and f.get("day")]
    priced = sorted(f["day"] for f in pays if f.get("amount"))
    dated = sorted(f["day"] for f in pays)
    first = priced[0] if priced else (dated[0] if dated else _date(got.get("first_investment")))
    first_out = _day_out(first) or _month_out(inv.get("named_month"))
    unfunded = _num(got.get("unfunded_commitment"))

    rows.append({
        "Investor entity": _text(got.get("investor_entity"), 160) or entity_folder,
        "Investment into": _text(got.get("investment_into"), 160) or folder,
        "Asset type": _text(got.get("asset_type"), 40),
        "Asset": _text(got.get("asset"), 240),
        "Commitment": _money(commitment, currency),
        "Unfunded commitment": _money(unfunded, currency) if unfunded is not None else "",
        "First investment": first_out,
        "Term": _text(got.get("term"), 400),
        "Holding period": _held(first, today),
        "Tax status": _text(got.get("tax_status"), 240),
        "Liquidity": _text(got.get("liquidity"), 300),
        "Currency": currency,
        "Website": _text(got.get("website"), 120),
        "General": "",
        "The business": _text(got.get("business")),
        "The investment": _text(got.get("investment")),
        "Notes": _text(got.get("notes"), 1200),
        "_folder": folder,
        "_entity_folder": entity_folder,
        "_url": str(inv.get("folder_url") or ""),
    })

    where = entity_folder + " / " + folder
    if not files:
        gaps.append([where, "The folder holds no files at all.",
                     "Nothing can be verified. Ask for the documents, or delete the folder."])
    # The term and how an investor gets out are settled in a deed, an agreement or a memorandum. A folder
    # of subscription forms and capital calls does not hold them, and no amount of reading will find them.
    if texts and not _text(got.get("term")) and not _text(got.get("liquidity")):
        gaps.append([where, "No document in the folder says how long this runs or how the money comes back "
                            "out, so Term and Liquidity could not be filled in.",
                     "The limited partnership agreement, trust deed or placement memorandum states both. "
                     "Add it to the folder, or type the two cells in once and they will be kept."])
    if not inv.get("named_month"):
        gaps.append([where, "The folder name does not start with a year and month.",
                     "Rename it to \"YYYY MM " + folder + "\" so the date comes from the name on every run."])
    if named is None:
        gaps.append([where, "The folder name does not state one clear amount, so the commitment had to be read "
                            "out of a document by AI.",
                     "Put the amount in the folder name, for example \"$400K\". The figure is then identical "
                     "on every run."])
    # A payment bigger than the whole investment is almost always filed in the wrong folder. The second
    # capital call for Fund 2, A$350,000, sits in the Year 13 folder, which is a A$100,000 investment.
    if named:
        for f in pays:
            if f.get("amount") and f["amount"] > named:
                gaps.append([where + " / " + f["path"],
                             "A payment of " + _money(f["amount"], currency) + " is filed here, but this folder "
                             "is for " + _money(named, currency) + ".",
                             "Check it belongs to this investment. A payment in the wrong folder is counted "
                             "against the wrong investment on every report."])
    if not any(f.get("category") == "Valuations" for f in files):
        gaps.append([where, "There is no capital account statement, holding statement or valuation in the folder.",
                     "Without one there is no carrying value, no MOIC and no IRR on any report."])
    for d in (inv.get("empty_drawers") or []):
        gaps.append([where, "The drawer \"" + d + "\" is empty.", "Expected for a new investment; otherwise the "
                                                                  "documents are filed somewhere else."])
    for u in unread[:4]:
        gaps.append([where, "Could not read " + u,
                     "A scan, an image or a signed PDF that is encrypted. Another document was read in its "
                     "place, so this row is not short because of it, but whatever only this file says is "
                     "missing. Replace it with the version that has text, or run it through OCR."])
    if len(unread) > 4:
        gaps.append([where, str(len(unread)) + " files in this folder could not be read as text, the four "
                            "above among them.",
                     "A folder whose deeds and valuations are all scans cannot have a term, a liquidity or a "
                     "carrying value read out of it, however many times this is run."])
    if inv.get("note"):
        gaps.append([where, str(inv.get("note")), "Check the folder opens in SharePoint."])

# One entity, one name. Only some of an entity's documents write out its full legal name, so without this
# the same investor is two investors in the register: the ones whose documents name it, and the ones left
# with the folder it sits in. The first investment that names it settles the name for all of them.
legal = {}
for r in rows:
    if r["_entity_folder"] not in legal and r["Investor entity"] != r["_entity_folder"]:
        legal[r["_entity_folder"]] = r["Investor entity"]
for r in rows:
    r["Investor entity"] = legal.get(r["_entity_folder"]) or r["Investor entity"]

# The same investment name under two different entities is the one mix-up a register cannot see for itself.
seen = {}
for r in rows:
    key = str(r["_folder"]).lower()
    seen.setdefault(key, []).append(str(r["Investor entity"]))
for key in seen:
    if len(seen[key]) > 1:
        gaps.append(["Across entities", "More than one entity holds a folder named \"" + key + "\": " +
                     ", ".join(seen[key]) + ".",
                     "Make sure any reference sheet matches on the entity as well as the folder name."])

summary = ("Read " + str(read_count) + " documents across " + str(len(rows)) + " investments and asked AI " +
           str(asked) + " of a possible " + str(len(rows) * len(QUESTIONS)) + " times, three questions per " +
           "investment: what was bought, the terms, then the descriptions. " +
           str(len(gaps)) + " gaps and queries raised.")

outputs.description: What is missing or needs a person to look at it.
outputs.name: gaps

nodes.summary: For each investment, reads the six documents most likely to carry the register's columns - terms, valuations, payments, tax, updates - and asks AI three questions about the lot: what was bought, the terms, the descriptions. Never one per document. Where a name states an amount or a day, it wins.

# -- Write the investment register to SharePoint as a new dated spreadsheet -- import base64 import re from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone from openpyxl import Workbook, load_workbook from openpyxl.styles import Alignment, Font, PatternFill from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter SP = "m365-sharepoint" SPW = "m365-sharepoint-write" FOLDER = "Investments/Reports" SHEET = "MySMB" GAPS_SHEET = "Gaps and queries" HEADERS = ["Investor entity", "Investment into", "Asset type", "Asset", "Commitment", "Unfunded commitment", "First investment", "Term", "Holding period", "Tax status", "Liquidity", "Currency", "Website", "General", "The business", "The investment", "Notes", "Folder"] WIDTHS = [30, 34, 12, 40, 14, 16, 14, 20, 14, 16, 34, 20, 26, 14, 52, 52, 70, 38] # Values a person has typed into the register are never overwritten by what AI reads next run. KEEP = ["Asset type", "Asset", "Commitment", "Unfunded commitment", "First investment", "Term", "Tax status", "Liquidity", "Currency", "Website", "General", "The business", "The investment", "Notes"] HEAD_FILL = "1F3864" MONTHS = ["", "Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"] def _err(exc): msg = str(exc) if msg.startswith("tool_error: "): msg = msg[len("tool_error: "):] if "no usable credential" in msg or "credential unavailable" in msg: return ("the connection that writes to SharePoint needs connecting (Settings - Connections - " "m365-sharepoint-write)") return msg[:300] def _norm(s): return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", str(s or "").lower()) def _key(entity, folder): return _norm(entity) + "|" + _norm(folder) def _d_fmt(d): return str(d.day).zfill(2) + "-" + MONTHS[d.month] + "-" + str(d.year)[2:] def _esc(s): return str(s or "").replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">") def _cell_text(v): if v is None: return "" if isinstance(v, date): return str(v.day).zfill(2) + "/" + str(v.month).zfill(2) + "/" + str(v.year) return str(v).strip() def _style_header(ws, widths): for c in ws[1]: c.font = Font(bold=True, color="FFFFFF") c.fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor=HEAD_FILL) c.alignment = Alignment(vertical="center") for i, w in enumerate(widths, start=1): ws.column_dimensions[get_column_letter(i)].width = w for line in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2): for c in line: c.alignment = Alignment(vertical="top", wrap_text=True) ws.freeze_panes = "A2" rows = params.get("rows") or [] gaps = params.get("gaps") or [] top_name = str(params.get("top_name") or "") problem = str(params.get("problem") or "") link = str(params.get("register_link") or "").strip() # The run happens on a server keeping UTC, and a register of Australian funds should be dated the day it # is in Australia. Without this a run late in the evening names its file for yesterday. today = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(hours=10)).date() register_file = "" report_link = "" kept = 0 added = 0 updated = 0 was_rows = 0 saved_as = "" trouble = "" # -- The workbook as it stands -------------------------------------------------------------------------- wb = None item = {} if link and rows: try: got = api.connectors.invoke(server=SPW, tool="read_sharepoint_file_bytes", args={"url": link}) got = got if isinstance(got, dict) else {} item = got.get("file") or {} raw = base64.b64decode(str(got.get("content_base64") or "")) path = api.files.scratch_path("register_in.xlsx") with open(path, "wb") as fh: fh.write(raw) wb = load_workbook(path) except Exception as exc: trouble = "Couldn't open the register in SharePoint: " + _err(exc) elif not link: trouble = ("No register link: paste the link of the spreadsheet to populate (Share - Copy link) when you " "click Run now.") if wb is not None: ws = wb[SHEET] if SHEET in wb.sheetnames else (wb.worksheets[0] if wb.worksheets else wb.create_sheet(SHEET)) # The headings as the spreadsheet writes them, so a column it already has is filled rather than repeated. head = [_cell_text(c.value) for c in ws[1]] if ws.max_row >= 1 else [] at = {} for i, name in enumerate(head): if _norm(name) and _norm(name) not in at: at[_norm(name)] = i + 1 width = len(head) for name in HEADERS: if _norm(name) not in at: width += 1 at[_norm(name)] = width ws.cell(row=1, column=width, value=name) # -- What is already in it --------------------------------------------------------------------------- held = {} alone = {} where_row = {} for r in range(2, ws.max_row + 1): was = {} for name in HEADERS: was[name] = _cell_text(ws.cell(row=r, column=at[_norm(name)]).value) if not (was.get("Investor entity") or was.get("Folder")): continue was_rows += 1 # Indexed under the folder name AND the investment name. A register kept by hand has no Folder # column in it yet, so matching on the folder alone would treat every row a person had already # filled in as a row that never existed, and write straight over it. for other in (was.get("Folder"), was.get("Investment into")): if other: if _key(was.get("Investor entity"), other) not in held: held[_key(was.get("Investor entity"), other)] = was where_row[_key(was.get("Investor entity"), other)] = r alone.setdefault(_norm(other), []).append((was, r)) # -- Fill it in -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- next_row = ws.max_row + 1 for row in rows: at_row = None was = None for other in (row.get("_folder"), row.get("Investment into")): k = _key(row.get("Investor entity"), other) if k in held: was, at_row = held[k], where_row[k] break # Last resort: the entity is written differently on the two sides - "Rapaki Pty Ltd ATF Rapaki Share # Trust" against the folder it sits in - and the folder name belongs to one row only. if was is None: for other in (row.get("_folder"), row.get("Investment into")): near = alone.get(_norm(other)) or [] if len(near) == 1: was, at_row = near[0] break if at_row is None: at_row = next_row next_row += 1 added += 1 else: updated += 1 for name in HEADERS: fresh = str(row.get("_folder") or "") if name == "Folder" else str(row.get(name) or "") mine = (was or {}).get(name) or "" if mine and name in KEEP: if mine.strip() != fresh.strip(): kept += 1 continue if fresh: ws.cell(row=at_row, column=at[_norm(name)], value=fresh) _style_header(ws, WIDTHS[:max(len(WIDTHS), width)] + [24] * max(0, width - len(WIDTHS))) # -- The gaps behind it ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ if GAPS_SHEET in wb.sheetnames: del wb[GAPS_SHEET] gs = wb.create_sheet(GAPS_SHEET) gs.append(["Folder or file", "What was found", "What to do about it"]) for g in gaps: gs.append([str(x or "") for x in (list(g) + ["", "", ""])[:3]]) _style_header(gs, [46, 76, 66]) out = api.files.scratch_path("register_out.xlsx") wb.save(out) with open(out, "rb") as fh: data = fh.read() # The spreadsheet that was pointed at is a template and is never written to. Each run saves a new file # beside it with the day in its name, so the template stays as it is however many times this is run, # and nothing has to be downloaded again to run it a second time. base = re.sub(r"\.xlsx$", "", str(item.get("name") or "Register"), flags=re.I) if item.get("parentId") and item.get("driveId"): # A name already in the folder gets a number rather than being replaced, so a result still being # looked at survives the next run the same morning. taken = [] try: listed = api.connectors.invoke(server=SP, tool="list_sharepoint_folder", args={"drive_id": item["driveId"], "item_id": item["parentId"]}) taken = [str(i.get("name") or "").lower() for i in ((listed or {}).get("items") or []) if isinstance(i, dict)] except Exception: taken = [] stem = base + " " + _d_fmt(today) written_as = stem + ".xlsx" nth = 2 while written_as.lower() in taken and nth < 60: written_as = stem + " (" + str(nth) + ").xlsx" nth += 1 try: wrote = api.connectors.invoke(server=SPW, tool="write_sharepoint_file", args={"drive_id": item["driveId"], "item_id": item["parentId"], "file_name": written_as, "content_base64": base64.b64encode(data).decode("ascii")}) wrote = wrote if isinstance(wrote, dict) else {} register_file = str((wrote.get("file") or {}).get("webUrl") or link) saved_as = written_as except Exception as exc: trouble = "Couldn't write the register to SharePoint: " + _err(exc) else: trouble = ("Couldn't work out which folder the spreadsheet is in, so nothing was written to " "SharePoint. There is a copy in Knowledge.") # Knowledge keeps a copy of exactly what went up, so there is a record even when SharePoint refuses. try: api.files.put(file=FOLDER + "/" + base + " " + _d_fmt(today) + ".xlsx", scratch_file=out) except Exception: pass entities = [] for row in rows: if row.get("Investor entity") and row["Investor entity"] not in entities: entities.append(row["Investor entity"]) # Reports shows HTML, not spreadsheets, so the register goes up there as a page people can read without # opening Excel. The spreadsheet in SharePoint stays the one that is kept. name = (top_name or "Investments") + " Investment Register " + _d_fmt(today) head_cells = "".join("" + _esc(h) + "" for h in HEADERS[:9]) body_rows = "" for row in rows: body_rows += "" + "".join("" + _esc(row.get(h)) + "" for h in HEADERS[:9]) + "" gap_rows = "".join("" + _esc(g[0]) + "" + _esc(g[1] if len(g) > 1 else "") + "" + _esc(g[2] if len(g) > 2 else "") + "" for g in gaps) page_html = ( "" + _esc(name) + "

" + _esc(name) + "

" + str(len(rows)) + " investments across " + str(len(entities)) + " entities, read from " + _esc(top_name) + ". The spreadsheet itself is in SharePoint.

" "" + head_cells + "" + body_rows + "
" "

Gaps and queries (" + str(len(gaps)) + ")

" "" + gap_rows + "
Folder or fileWhat was foundWhat to do about it
") html_path = api.files.scratch_path("register.html") with open(html_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh: fh.write(page_html) try: made = api.artifacts.put(title=name, scratch_file=html_path, file_name=name + ".html", kind="document", visibility="tenant", mime_type="text/html", description="Every investment held across " + str(len(entities)) + " entities, read from the SharePoint folders.", tags=["investment register", (top_name or "Investments")[:40]]) report_link = str((made or {}).get("url") or "") if isinstance(made, dict) else "" except Exception: report_link = "" if problem and not rows: summary = problem elif trouble: summary = trouble else: summary = ("Wrote " + ("\"" + saved_as + "\"" if saved_as else "the register") + " to SharePoint beside " + "the one it was built from, with " + str(updated) + " row" + ("" if updated == 1 else "s") + " filled in and " + str(added) + " added, across " + str(len(entities)) + " entities. " + str(kept) + " cell" + ("" if kept == 1 else "s") + " already filled in by hand " + ("was" if kept == 1 else "were") + " carried over as " + ("it" if kept == 1 else "they") + " stood. " + str(len(gaps)) + " gaps and queries are on the " + GAPS_SHEET + " sheet. " + "The spreadsheet it was built from is unchanged.")

Each run saves a new file beside it with the day in its name, so this one can be used again and again without being put back. Every cell already filled in there is carried into the new file exactly as it is and only the empty ones are written, so what a person has decided is never overwritten by what AI reads. Rows are matched on the investor entity and the folder name together.
